A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiCE/SPN-MIO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original five-fold Adult experiments in Table 1 and additional distance and sparsity results in Appendix B, Tables 7–8.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on Adult, Give Me Some Credit and German Credit, including benchmark comparisons, LiCE variants and timing results in Tables 2–3 and 9–11.

M1.justification: The central mixed-polytope, classifier and approximate SPN formulation remains. v2 adds a factual-dependent likelihood-threshold variant in A.5.2 and integer-domain constraints for normalized discrete features in A.2.6. The weighted likelihood objective develops an option already mentioned in v1.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from Adult alone to Adult, Give Me Some Credit and German Credit. The two additional credit datasets substantially broaden the represented data and feature types; German Credit also replaces Adult in the illustrative case study.

E2.justification: PROPLACE becomes an evaluated comparator alongside the retained DiCE, VAE, C-CHVAE, FACE variants and MIO. The closest-only MIO comparison reported in v1 Tables 7–8 disappears. PlaCE and DACE remain unevaluated despite appearing in v2's capability comparison.

E3.justification: Plausibility evaluation changes from tuned KDE log-density to SPN negative log-likelihood. Adult changes from 32,561 samples and eight features to 47,876 samples and nine features; classifier hidden layers change from 15/10 to 20/10. Candidate selection changes from prioritizing valid-and-actionable CEs to selecting the likeliest valid CE. Timing changes from means over successful valid CEs to medians over all attempts. Five-fold evaluation and 100 factuals per fold remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic comparisons of median, quartile, factual-dependent and weighted-objective LiCE variants in Table 10, substantially expanding analysis of the likelihood–distance tradeoff. The earlier closest-versus-likeliest MIO analysis is removed, and Figure 1 replaces the Adult case study with a German Credit example.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-fold cross-validation and mean-plus/minus-dispersion tables. v2 Table 3 explicitly identifies the dispersion as standard deviation, whereas v1 leaves the plus/minus quantities unnamed. This clarifies reporting without establishing additional repetitions or new significance testing.

E6.justification: Benchmark results are extensively replaced and expanded. Adult LiCE's reported valid/actionable rates change from 51.6%/51.6% in v1 Table 1 to 92.4%/62.6% for LiCE(median) in v2 Table 2 under revised settings. New GMSC results show strong threshold sensitivity: 3.2% valid for LiCE(median) versus 100% for LiCE(quartile). New datasets, PROPLACE and additional variants also introduce substantial new result entries.

T1.justification: The original SPN approximation bound and most validity, sparsity and causal constraints are retained or relocated. v2 adds the discrete-feature integrality constraint in A.2.6 and an assertion that hard-EM training makes the sum-node approximation exact in Section 3, without adding a proof of that assertion.

C1.justification: The central SPN-in-MIO and LiCE contributions remain. The abstract and introduction change the comparative framing from distance-focused explanations being implausible to plausibility-focused methods sacrificing proximity, and explicitly claim simultaneous likelihood, closeness and sparsity. This refines the claimed advantage within the existing contribution.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes leading KDE plausibility and discusses FACE outliers and LiCE's sparsity shortcomings. v2 recasts the empirical message around similarity and sparsity with comparable likelihood, and emphasizes the strength of two-stage MIO selection. It adds substantive explanations and qualifications concerning threshold-dependent failures, small-dataset difficulties, possible VAE misconfiguration, questionable GMSC timings and rejection of KDE for categorical data.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 add extensive preprocessing rules, dataset-specific constraints, training and SPN hyperparameters, numerical margins, solving limits, hardware and compute information. v2 reports using OMLT/Pyomo and supplies a repository link where v1 promised future release. Appendix A.4 nevertheless retains inconsistent future-release wording; actual repository availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted positioning around PROPLACE and counterfactual disagreement, plus implementation and piecewise-modeling references. Table 1 introduces a method-capability comparison, and A.2 newly claims originality for the desiderata formulations. Explanations for excluding PlaCE and DACE are revised, while the broader relationship to MIO and tractable probabilistic models remains.

P1.justification: SPN encoding becomes a standalone section before the LiCE method, while detailed formulations move into Appendix A.2. The former appendices A–C are reorganized into A.1–A.6. The abstract, motivating example, experimental narrative and discussion are substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds a capability matrix and redraws Figure 1 with different data, axes, markers and legend placement. Results are reorganized into separate success-rate, multi-dataset quality, variant and timing tables, replacing the earlier table organization. The five notation tables largely carry over with revised caption placement.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the work more reproducible and informative through detailed experimental documentation and comparisons that expose threshold sensitivity beyond Adult. However, it replaces v1's separate KDE plausibility check with the SPN already guiding generation and selection, reducing independent validation. A.5–A.6 also acknowledge questionable timings and possible baseline misconfiguration. The documentation and diagnostic gains support a net improvement, but these unresolved evaluation weaknesses limit its overall magnitude.
